verdict.rationale: Crossplane's official CLI can render and test Composition Functions headlessly, without a cluster. That gives an agent a way to preview the resources a change would produce (crossplane-docs-7, crossplane-probe-1). Its declarative APIs are explicitly pitched as safe for AI agents to act on (crossplane-docs-54, crossplane-docs-16). Nothing in the evidence shows a plan that diffs proposed changes against live infrastructure state, or a documented approval gate before apply; the helm dry-run applies only to installing Crossplane itself. Missing for 10: a documented plan/diff against live state, an approval-before-apply workflow, an agent-driven authoring flow, and hands-on corroboration.
